mechanism.plausibility_rationale: Tendon rupture is not a commonly reported side effect of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs). SSRIs primarily work by inhibiting the reuptake of serotonin into the presynaptic neuron, thereby increasing the availability of serotonin in the synaptic cleft. This mechanism of action is not directly linked to the musculoskeletal system or tendon integrity. While some side effects of SSRIs can include gastrointestinal issues, sexual dysfunction, and changes in weight, tendon rupture is not typically associated with their use. Therefore, the plausibility of tendon rupture as a side effect of SSRIs is considered low.
